page: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the Esv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. A key characteristic of this server is its high memory density, providing 512.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 32.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in specific memory and compression tasks. The server achieves a strong rating in large-block memory write bandwidth at 90.18 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 31.31 GB/sec. Geekbench testing shows a strong single-core score of 2115.0 and a strong text processing score of 2640.0. Other metrics, such as stress-ng CPU performance, multi-core Geekbench, and Redis SET operations at 22.37 million operations per second, fall within the average range. For small LLM inference using a 135M model, it delivers a strong text generation speed of 288.15 tokens per second.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per vCPU, this instance offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without requiring the purchase of excess compute cores. This makes it a cost-efficient choice for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications. The lack of local storage means workloads must rely on external Premium Storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. It is highly suited for memory-intensive database operations, data analytics, and memory-cached web serving.
